translations.text: The words of the Lord that came to Joel son of Bethuel.
Listen to these things, elder, and [?]
Put on sackcloth, priests, and mourn. Lament, you who serve at the altar. Go inside and sleep in sackcloth, you who serve God, because sacrifices and drink offerings have ceased in the house of God.
Consecrate a fast and proclaim a service of worship. Gather the elders and everyone who lives in the land into the house of the Lord, and cry out loudly, saying:
Woe to me! Woe to me because of the day of the Lord! For the day of the Lord is near, and it will come like misery.
Has not food been taken away before you, and joy and gladness from the house of your God?
I will throw everyone who lives on the earth into turmoil, because the day of the Lord has come.

For a day of darkness and gloom is approaching, a day of clouds and thick mist. Like the dawn, a numerous and powerful people will spread over the mountains. Nothing like them has existed from the beginning, and after them nothing like them will exist for generations upon generations.
Before him is a devouring fire, and behind him is a blazing flame.
And the sky will shake. The sun and the moon will grow dark, and the stars will not give their light.
And the Lord will raise his voice before his army, because the day of the Lord is very great. It is great, terrifying, and manifest, and who will be able to endure it?
[?] the wine and the oil, and you will be satisfied with them. And I will no longer make you an object of ridicule among the nations.

And I will drive the one from the north away from you and cast him into a land without water. I will destroy his front in the eastern sea and his rear in the western sea. His decay will rise up, [?] his stench will rise up, because he has increased his deeds.
Land, take courage! Rejoice and be glad, because the Lord has exalted himself to act.
You beasts of the field, take courage, for the plants of the wilderness have sprouted. The tree has brought forth its fruit; the vine and the fig tree have yielded their abundance.
Children of Zion, rejoice and be glad in the Lord your God, because he has given you food in righteousness. And he will send you the early and the late rain, as before.
And the threshing floors will be full of grain, and the vats will overflow with wine and oil.
I will repay you for the years that the locust, the young locusts, the blight, and the caterpillar consumed—my great army that I sent against you.
And you will eat abundantly and be satisfied, and you will praise the name of the Lord your God for the wonderful things he has done for you. And my people will never be put to shame.
You will know that I am in the midst of [?], and that I am the Lord your God, and there is no other besides me. From now on, my people will never be put to shame.
And afterward it will happen that I will pour out from my [?] upon all flesh. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy, your old people will dream dreams, and your young people will see visions.
Also upon my male slaves and my female slaves in those days I will pour out from my [?], and they will prophesy.
And I will give wonders in heaven above and signs below on the earth: blood, fire, and a cloud of smoke.
The sun will turn to darkness and the moon to blood before the great and manifest day of the Lord comes.

And it will happen that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved. For those who are saved will be on Mount Zion and in [?], because the Lord has said it, and the one who brings good news to those whom the Lord has called.
For look: in those days and at that time, when I bring back the captives of Judah and Jerusalem,

I will gather all the nations and bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat. I will judge them there concerning my people and my inheritance, [?], whom they scattered among the nations. And they divided my land among themselves.
They cast lots for my people and gave the little boys for a [?]. They sold the little girls for wine and drank it.

And what do you have to do with me, Tyre and Sidon and all Galilee of the Philistines? Are you going to repay me with repayment, or are you planning evil against me? Swiftly and without delay I will bring your repayment upon your own heads.
For you have taken my silver and my gold, and you have brought my choice and beautiful things into your temples.
And you sold the children of Judah and the children of [?] to the children of [?], so that you could drive them away from their own territories.
Look, I will raise them up from the place to which you sold them, and I will bring your repayment upon your own heads.
And I will hand your sons and your daughters over to the children of Judah, and they will sell them into captivity to a nation living far away, because the Lord has spoken.
Proclaim these things among the nations: Consecrate a war; rouse the warriors. Advance and go up, all men, all men who are warriors.
Beat your plowshares into swords and your sickles into spears. Let the weak person say, “I am strong.”
Gather together and come in, all the surrounding nations. Gather yourselves there. Let the gentle person become a warrior.
Let all the surrounding nations rise and go up. Gather yourselves there. Let the gentle person become a warrior.
Send out your sickles, for the harvest is near. Go in and tread, for the winepress is full, and the vats are overflowing, because their wickedness has increased.
Voices cried out in the valley of judgment, and the day of the Lord is near in the valley of judgment.
The sun and the moon will grow dark, and the stars will not give their light.
The Lord will cry out from Zion and send out his voice from [?]. Heaven and earth will shake. But the Lord will spare his people and give strength to the children of [?].
Then you will know that I am the Lord your God, dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain. And [?] will become a holy city, and foreigners will no longer pass through it.

On that day the mountains will drip sweet wine, and the hills will flow with milk. All the watercourses of Judah will send out their water, and a spring will come out from the house of the Lord and water the ravine of thorns.
Egypt will become a ruin, and Idumea a ruined wilderness, because of the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed the blood of righteous people in their land.
But Idumea will be inhabited forever, and [?] for generations upon generations.
I will avenge their blood, which I have not forgiven. [?] The Lord will dwell in Zion.
